title: Applet: state of presentation mode switch is not synchronized across multiple instances
line: Turning presentation mode on or off in one Display Configuration widget now updates the switch in every other one.
explanation: The presentation mode switch state was a plain property of each applet's QML, set only by that applet's own switch. The inhibition cookie itself is already shared within plasmashell by the powermanagement engine, but a second widget had no way to know the mode was on, so its switch stayed off (and the applet filters plasmashell's own inhibition out of its hint). The change adds a presentationModeEnabled property to the applet's C++ class backed by a static value that notifies every instance; the switches and the applet's active status/tooltip bind to it.

commits.message:
plasmoid: share presentation mode state between applet instances

Each Display Configuration widget kept its own presentation mode state, so
enabling it in one left the switch off in every other one. Store the state
in the applet class, shared by all instances, and bind the switches to it.

BUG: 426426

media.caption: Presentation mode enabled in the desktop widget; the tray's Display Configuration switch is still off.
Same steps with the fix: the tray's switch is on too, and the tray icon shows presentation mode is active.

review.text: Clean, concise fix that stores presentation mode state on KScreenApplet and notifies all live applet instances, synchronizing the switch, active tray status, and tooltip across multiple widgets. Binding PresentationModeItem.checked and updating the shared property from onToggled preserves the QML binding without triggering duplicate PowerDevil calls, and ~KScreenApplet() cleanly unregisters destroyed instances. Evidence and regression checks match the diff well.

reviews.text: Clean, concise fix that stores presentation mode state on KScreenApplet and notifies all live applet instances, synchronizing the switch, active tray status, and tooltip across multiple widgets. Binding PresentationModeItem.checked and updating the shared property from onToggled preserves the QML binding without triggering duplicate PowerDevil calls, and ~KScreenApplet() cleanly unregisters destroyed instances. Evidence and regression checks match the diff well.

This fixes the reported desync: presentation mode state now lives in one value inside plasmashell, shared by every Display Configuration instance. All instances use the same inhibition cookie in the powermanagement engine, so turning it off from another instance really removes the inhibition (checked in the verify notes). The switch binds to the shared property and writes it only on onToggled, which avoids the old onCheckedChanged feedback. The static applet list is simple, with no lifetime risk, since instances remove themselves in the destructor. Deriving the state from PowerDevil's real inhibitions would be more robust, but this is the singleton Nate asked for and is fine as is.
